trajectory: Yes: the same piece of state is patched again. Clips `switchTo` has now been reshaped in three successive rounds. r2→r3 widened the predicate that clears it (`switchedAway` became `switchSettled`, with a `view.view === "home"` disjunct). This round (191990387 → knowledge b64999b) changes its type from a target id to `{ id, search }`. That adds a snapshot of the URL at the time of the choice, which acts as a prediction that the viewer is 'still on it'. A derived `switchPending` (`switchTo.search === search`) replaces the plain `switchTo !== null` in the effectiveParams, fill-in and switchHref conditions. The round also removed things: the `view.view === "home"` disjunct, and the setting of `switchTo` at all when the choice is made on Home (chooseTarget now sets it only off Home). On net it swaps one condition for another and does not reduce state. The transient flags (`switchTo` in Clips, `switchingFor` in Notes) are still in place. Notes is untouched this round.

findings.claim: After a Target change, Clips and Notes clear their transient switch flag in the same effect that calls `router.replace`. In the real Next.js app router the replace is a transition and commits after the flag update, so one render shows the new Target with the previous Target's URL `group`/`sort` and sends a Library request with them.
findings.impact: The viewer chooses another Target on the Clips Library, or on the Notes Library. The Library briefly redraws with the old Target's grouping and sort, sends a shelves or list request with them, and then switches to the new Target's view when the URL update lands. That is a flicker plus one wasted request under a view that is not the one finally shown.
findings.evidence: clips.tsx:213-221: `router.replace(switchHref); setSwitchTo(null);`. On the next commit `switchTo` is null, so `switchPending` (clips.tsx:154) is false and `effectiveParams` (155-162) keeps the old URL's `group`/`sort`. `readClipsView` (163) then yields the previous Target's view. `bodyDrawn` is true, and `Library` (293-303) mounts `useGroupShelves` with that view, which fires a request. `fillHref` (256-259) stays null because the old URL is readable. Notes has the same pattern: NotesPage.tsx `setSwitchingFor(null); router.replace(...)`, after which `ignoreUrlSort` is false and NotesLibrary reads the URL's old sort for its list request. The test harness hides this. notesAppHarness.tsx:44-79 implements replace as a synchronous `useSyncExternalStore` update, so the search change and the flag change land in the same render.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Traced under Next.js semantics, where app-router push/replace run inside startTransition and a plain setState in the same effect commits first. Store {"sf-work":{"group":"none"}}, open `?view=all&group=folder&sort=title`, choose Work. Expected requests are by=all/none only. By the trace, one `by=folder&sort=title` shelves request under Work's conditions goes out between the switch render and the URL commit.

bucket_proposal.reason: I8: after a Target change, no Library body request is sent with a grouping or sort other than the one finally shown for that Target.

findings.proposed_fix: Keep the flag until the URL actually reflects the replacement: clear `switchTo` only when `search` changes, which the `!switchPending` branch of `switchSettled` already does. Drop the eager `setSwitchTo(null)` after `router.replace`. Do the same for `switchingFor` in NotesPage.

findings.claim: When a Clips Target is chosen on the Library and the chosen member Target then evaluates to `tooLarge`/`failed`, `default` is put in force and `switchTo` is cleared without a rewrite. The URL keeps the previous Target's `group`/`sort`.
findings.impact: The viewer on Target Y picks member Target X, and X turns out unusable. The page shows `default`, but with Y's grouping and sort from the URL instead of default's stored view. Back and forth then mixes Y's view into default's Library.
findings.evidence: useNotesTarget.ts:162-166: `selectedId` becomes 'default' once `unusableMember` is true. clips.tsx:211-212: `switchSettled` is true when `target.status === "ready" && targetId !== switchTo.id`, so the effect at 213-217 only clears `switchTo`. effectiveParams then keeps the old `group`/`sort`.

bucket_proposal.reason: The spec says a fallback to `default` leaves the URL alone, but I4 says no view parameter is left over from the previous Target after a switch. This case sits between the two and the spec does not settle it.
